items.title: Waste picker in Bengaluru set ablaze after being tied up, in critical condition
items.summary: A 45-year-old waste picker is in critical condition after unidentified persons allegedly tied him up, poured petrol on him, and set him ablaze on a road in Veerabhadranagar, south Bengaluru, in the early hours of Wednesday, November 18. The victim, identified as Mohammed alias Syed H, was found by area residents around 6 am, with severe burn injuries. They alerted the police through the emergency helpline 112. A Hoysala patrol team reached the spot and arranged for an ambulance to shift him to Victoria Hospital, where he is undergoing treatment. According to the police, Mohammed has suffered 60-70% burns. His hands and legs were allegedly tied with ropes before he was set on fire. Mohammed collects scrap for a living and has no permanent shelter, mobile phone, or identity documents. He reportedly sleeps on the roadside and had been staying in the Padarayanapura area for several years. Girinagar police visited the spot and are investigating the incident. A case is being registered, the police said.

items.title: TVK under fire after cadres open Theni dam outlet without govt order, share videos
items.summary: The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) is facing criticism after some of its functionaries allegedly opened a water outlet connected to the Sothuparai dam in Theni district without the knowledge or permission of government officials and shared videos of the incident on social media. The incident took place on Tuesday, November 17, near Periyakulam, where the functionaries, led by TVK's Theni North-East district joint secretary Sheikh Ali, opened a water outlet in an irrigation channel, claiming that they had acted on the instructions of Periyakulam MLA Sabari Aingaran to benefit around 1,000 acres of farmland. Water Resources Department (WRD) officials told The Hindu that the functionaries had not opened the main shutters of the Sothuparai dam. Instead, they opened a water outlet in the New Canal located around 1.5 km downstream of the dam to divert excess water overflowing from the reservoir. It has to be noted that the irrigation structure was under the direct control of the WRD and that no outsider could operate it without permission.
